req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the PUT operation should be idempotent, meaning that repeated requests with the same data should not alter the state beyond the initial application. This is crucial for ensuring consistency in RESTful APIs. The test suite includes a positive test to verify correct behavior, a negative test to ensure proper error handling, and a boundary test to check edge cases.

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_positive
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 1
Send the same PUT request again
expected: Task state remains unchanged after second request
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Initial PUT request
response1 = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 5", "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbo…", "completed": True}
)
assert response1.status_code == 200

# Repeated PUT request
response2 = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 5", "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbo…", "completed": True}
)
assert response2.status_code == 200

# Verify idempotency
assert response1.json() == response2.json()

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_negative
preconditions: Task with id 999 does not exist in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update non-existent task with id 999
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Attempt to update a non-existent task
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/999",
    json={"title": "Non-existent task", "description": "This task does not exist.", "completed": False}
)
assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 999 not found"

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_boundary
preconditions: Task with id 2 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT request with maximum length description to update task with id 2
expected: Task is updated with maximum length description
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Update task with maximum length description
max_length_description = "X" * 500
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/2",
    json={"title": "Book flight tickets", "description": max_length_description, "completed": True}
)
assert response.status_code == 200

# Verify the update
updated_task = response.json()
assert updated_task["description"] == max_length_description
